facts: A walled chamber (Warehouse Walls), 11 x 8 m, stands inside the room; you enter it through a 1.8 m opening in its side.
Three low monoliths (Drifting Product Plinths) inside it carry the product at 0.9-1.4 m high.
Two blocks (Piercing Rusty Beams) break through the chamber walls on opposite sides.
The pay desk (Harbor Cash Desk) and the fitting room (Fitting Block) stay outside the chamber.
anchors: outside the chamber, where a block breaks through its wall; you look at the Piercing Rusty Beams (rock)
inside the chamber, facing its back wall; you look at the Warehouse Walls (mirror_wall)
beside a monolith; you look at the Drifting Product Plinths (display)

args.title: HARBOR SHADOWS: THE POP-UP
args.subtitle: A transient collection in a harbor’s hold.
args.line: A desolate harbor warehouse where the rhythmic sweep of a lighthouse beam illuminates the cargo of time.
args.synopsis: You step into the damp, echoing shell of a warehouse lost to the sea. Inside the central chamber, the Drifting Product Plinths emerge from the dense mist, holding artifacts as if they were salvaged cargo. A flickering warmth glides over the surfaces, mimicking the lighthouse that guides ghosts home. Here, the boundary between storage and sanctuary dissolves in the fog.
args.quote: Memory is a beacon that cuts through the fog of the present.

why.d: The enclosing walls create a sense of being lost at sea within a confined industrial space.
The low plinths make you lean in close, as if examining treasures washed up by the tide.
These heavy protrusions puncture the space, suggesting the relentless force of the harbor environment.
Keeping the transaction and fitting processes external separates the sacred act of viewing from the routine.
